A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPQE study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including material reorganized or expanded in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval experiments comparing DeepRetrieval, SPQE, and OPQE, including benchmark scores in Tables 1–4 and training trajectories in Figure 1.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports backbone-matched SPQE scores, output-length measurements, and generated-query case studies.

M1.justification: OPQE still uses PPO to optimize pseudo-document generation, concatenating the original query with the generated passage. Algorithm 1, objectives, rewards, and appendix prompt templates are retained. New prompt-design and corpus-adaptation explanations do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same evidence-seeking, MS MARCO/TREC/BEIR, and ToolRet datasets. Appendix dataset statistics are unchanged. New length measurements and cases use existing datasets; multi-turn search and other proposed extensions remain future work.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds explicit SPQE-3B and SPQE-7B comparators using the Qwen2.5 backbones matched to DeepRetrieval. v2 mentioned these only as preliminary experiments. Appendix B adds their detailed comparisons, while retaining the existing unaugmented, DeepRetrieval, and stronger-model SPQE comparators.

E3.justification: The new length analysis measures output characters excluding reasoning tokens (Table 5). Core retrieval metrics, splits, and PPO hyperparameters are retained. Appendix tool tables identify the dense retriever as E5-base-v2 instead of Contriever-msmarco, aligning with Section 4.4 but still conflicting with main Tables 2–3; this does not establish an actual retriever switch or rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: quantitative backbone-matched comparisons assess model-capacity effects, Table 5 examines output length across three datasets, and Figures 2, 7, and 8 compare answer-bearing terms and verbosity in NQ examples. v2 supplied preliminary qualitative backbone remarks and reward trajectories. No length-matched causal ablation is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 1 gains smoothed display lines without a newly specified uncertainty procedure; output-length averages are descriptive results rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds matched-backbone results across all three task families, plus length measurements and case outputs. For example, Table 1 newly reports SPQE-7B ad hoc NDCG@10 averages of 47.7 with BM25 and 53.9 with Contriever-msmarco. All retained Table 1 scores and Tables 2–4 remain unchanged; these additions do not represent improved OPQE performance between versions.

T1.justification: Equation 1, the reward formulations, and the completeness definition in Appendices C–D are unchanged. Added discussion of verifiable rewards and on-policy versus preference-based optimization is conceptual positioning, without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and concluding findings retain the same claims: a compute-aware comparison, competitive prompting with capable LLMs, and OPQE’s hybrid advantage. Expanded agentic-search motivation and PPO scope explanations do not redefine those core contributions.

C2.justification: Sections 4.5 and 5.2 replace the symmetric document-to-document explanation with richer semantic specification and retriever-distribution alignment. v3 adds an elicitation-versus-acquisition interpretation, deployment-cost conditions, and case-based explanations. It also develops the existing caution about coupled format, length, and content, while expanding applicability boundaries and future directions.

D1.justification: v3 specifies eight A100 GPUs for 3B policies and sixteen for 7B, resolving the earlier illustrative 7–14 GPU statement against the already reported 8/16 setup. Section 5.1 additionally specifies newline concatenation and explains corpus adaptation and index updates. The code link, framework, main hyperparameters, and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The research positioning expands substantially to agentic search, off-policy preference optimization, RLVR, and reasoning faithfulness. New discussions connect OPQE to Search-R1, ReasonIR, ParallelSearch, Rec-R1, and related work, positioning query augmentation as an individual action complementary to retriever improvements and search orchestration.

P1.justification: v3 substantially expands and rewrites the motivation, scope explanation, discussion, method exposition, and future-work narrative. It introduces several explanatory subheadings and Appendix F while preserving the main section sequence. Author and publication-header changes accompany this broader editorial revision.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains matched-backbone columns, appendix SPQE comparisons are reorganized into matched-backbone and stronger-model tables, and a length table and three case-study figures are added. Figure 1 is redrawn with prominent smoothed lines over faint raw trajectories. Existing prompt figures and other tables are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 makes v2’s preliminary backbone comparison numerically checkable and adds useful length measurements, examples, and interpretive qualifications. These improve transparency, but compute matching remains unquantified and causal factors remain entangled. Tool-retriever labels still conflict, and the new length discussion reports 113–130 characters despite Table 5 showing OPQE averages of 129–130. The net gain is useful but limited.
